result.title: Incremental Roseland: Batch-wise Landmark Diffusion via Kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève Update
result.summary: Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. It assumes, however, that all data are available at once. We introduce incremental Roseland (iRoseland), which casts the landmark affinity as a row-growing matrix whose SVD can be updated with a kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève (SKL) scheme. Degre correction is handled by a first order expansion about a reference mean kernel row and so that the landmark-side eigenbasis may be recovered from a single landmark-by-landmark eigendecomposition at each step. The presented method requires only a single pass over the data and runs in bounded-memory with state independent of the number of points processed. A forgetting factor lets the method track drifting distributions, and a sample-size-invariant embedding keeps outputs comparable across time. Experiments show agreement with Roseland to round-off on stationary data, and accuracy that exceeds equal-memory Roseland by an order of magnitude on long streams. On drifting data, we observe large gains from forgetting with a window matched to the drift.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 iRoseland，将 landmark diffusion 的亲和矩阵看作逐行增长的矩阵，用 kernelized Sequential Karhunen–Loève 方案增量更新其 SVD，实现对度数校正的一阶展开处理，并支持单遍、有界内存运行与遗忘因子跟踪分布漂移。
